The reciters of the major regional centres, with the exception of Abu Ja'far, read both the ﴿ilaf﴾ and the ﴿ilafihim﴾ with a yā' after the hamza. Abu Ja'far agreed with the others on ﴿ilaf﴾, reading it with a yā' after the hamza, but there are different reports about his reading of ﴿ilafihim﴾. It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ concerning this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting: "ilfahum rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf".

Alas for their fathers, from a ʿarif and a poet!

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿and secured them against fear﴾: when Abraham, peace be upon him, said ﴿My Lord, make this land secure﴾.

Others said: What is meant by this is: and He secured them from leprosy.

Those who said so:

⁕ al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all saying: al-Dahhak said: ﴿and secured them against fear﴾: from their fear of leprosy.

⁕ ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAmir ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿and secured them against fear﴾, he said: The fear is leprosy.

The correct statement on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that He ﴿secured them against fear﴾, and the enemy is a thing feared, and leprosy is a thing feared. So the correct view is that it should be general as He, exalted is His remembrance, made it general, and thus it is said: He secured them from both of these things.

Others said: What is meant by this is: and He secured them from leprosy.

Those who said so:

The correct statement on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that He ﴿secured them against fear﴾, and the enemy is a thing feared, and leprosy is a thing feared. So the correct view is that it should be general as He, exalted is His remembrance, made it general, and thus it is said: He secured them from both of these things.

End of the exegesis of Surat Quraysh.

The exegesis concerning His words, may His majesty and His names be exalted: ﴿For the covenant (ilaf) of the Quraysh, their covenant (ilafihim) of the caravan of winter and summer, let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear﴾.

The reciters (al-qurra', the transmitters of Qur'anic readings) differed over the reading of ﴿ilaf Quraysh ilafihim﴾. The reciters of the major regional centres, with the exception of Abu Ja'far, read both the ﴿ilaf﴾ and the ﴿ilafihim﴾ with a yā' after the hamza. Abu Ja'far agreed with the others on ﴿ilaf﴾, reading it with a yā' after the hamza, but there are different reports about his reading of ﴿ilafihim﴾. It is reported from him that he read it as "ilfihim" (إلْفِهِمْ), taking it as a verbal noun from alifa, yaʾlafu, ilfan, without a yā'. Some have related from him that he read it as "ilafihim" (إلافِهِمْ), without a yā' and with a short alif.

The correct reading in my view is the one that reads both with the yā' after the hamza, from ʾalaftu al-shay'a, ʾulifuhu, ilafan, because the reciters, who are the authoritative body, agree upon it. The Arabs have two usages: ʾalaftu and alaftu. Whoever says ʾalaftu with a long alif says "fa-ana ʾuʾālifu ilafan" (I am making a covenant); whoever says alaftu with a short alif says "fa-ana ʾālifu ilfan", and he is a man who is ʾālif ilfan (accustomed). It is related from ʿIkrimah that he used to read it: "li-tuʾlifa Quraysh ilfahum rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf" (that Quraysh may become accustomed to their journey of winter and summer).

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated this to me, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Makin, from ʿIkrimah.

It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ concerning this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting: "ilfahum rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf".

The grammarians (ahl al-ʿarabiyya) disagreed about the meaning that brings in this lām in His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: what governs it is His words ﴿so He made them like eaten chaff﴾. According to this view, the lām is connected to His words "made them", so the meaning of the speech must be: We did this to the People of the Elephant as a favour from Us to the people of this House and as a kindness from Us to them, in addition to Our favour upon them in the journey of winter and summer. Thus the lām in ﴿li-ilaf﴾ would mean "ilā" (to), as if it were said: a favour for a favour, and to a favour, because ilā stands in the place of lām and lām stands in the place of ilā.

Some of the exegetes (ahl al-taʾwil, those who interpret the Qur'an) have stated this view.

⁕ Isma'il ibn Musa al-Sudi narrated to me, saying: Sharik informed us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid: ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, who said: My favour upon Quraysh.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Hilali narrated to me, saying: Farwa ibn Abi al-Maghra' al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAmir ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, who said: My favour upon Quraysh.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: This view has been stated, and it is said that He, blessed and exalted, made His Prophet ﷺ marvel, so He said: Marvel, O Muhammad, at the blessings of God upon Quraysh, in their covenant of the journey of winter and summer. Then He said: Let them not occupy themselves with that from faith and from following you; the proof is in His words ﴿so let them worship the Lord of this House﴾.

Some of the exegetes directed the interpretation of His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾ toward the mutual affection of some of them for others.

Those who said so:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of God ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, and he recited ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the People of the Elephant?﴾ up to the end of the surah, and said: This is for the covenant of Quraysh. I did this to them for the affection of Quraysh, lest I disperse their affection and their union, and the People of the Elephant came only to seize their sacred ones; so God did that.

The correct statement on this matter, in our view, is that this lām carries the meaning of wonder (taʿajjub), and that the meaning of the speech is: Marvel at the covenant of Quraysh in the journey of winter and summer, and their abandoning the worship of the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear. So let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear. When the Arabs bring this lām into speech for wonder, they suffice with it as evidence of wonder at the appearance of the verb that it governs, as the poet said:

Alas for their fathers, from a ʿarif and a poet!

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh ilafihim﴾, who said: The people of Mecca were merchants who alternated this in winter and summer, secure among the Arabs, while the Arabs raided one another and could not do so against them, nor could they manage it, out of fear. Even if a man of them was struck in one of the Arab quarters, when someone said "a man of the sanctuary (Hirmi)" he was left alone along with his property, in honour of that, for the security God had given them.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, ﴿and secured them against fear﴾, who said: They used to say: We are of the sanctuary of God, so no one would confront them in the Jahiliyya, and they were secure by that; but other tribes of the Arabs, when they went out, were raided.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿and secured them against fear﴾: The Arabs raided one another and took one another captive, but they were secure from that because of the sanctuary. And he recited: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which the fruits of every thing are brought?﴾

Others said: What is meant by this is: and He secured them from leprosy.

Those who said so:

⁕ al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all saying: al-Dahhak said: ﴿and secured them against fear﴾: from their fear of leprosy.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, ﴿and secured them against fear﴾, who said: from leprosy and other things.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' said: I heard "who fed them against hunger": hunger. "And secured them against fear": fear is leprosy.

⁕ ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAmir ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿and secured them against fear﴾, he said: The fear is leprosy.

The correct statement on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that He ﴿secured them against fear﴾, and the enemy is a thing feared, and leprosy is a thing feared. God did not specify the report that He secured them from the enemy to the exclusion of leprosy, nor from leprosy to the exclusion of the enemy; rather He made the report general. So the correct view is that it should be general as He, exalted is His remembrance, made it general, and thus it is said: He secured them from both of these things.

End of the exegesis of Surat Quraysh.

The exegesis concerning His words, may His majesty and His names be exalted: ﴿For the covenant (ilaf) of the Quraysh, their covenant (ilafihim) of the caravan of winter and summer, let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear﴾.

The reciters (al-qurra', the transmitters of Qur'anic readings) differed over the reading of ﴿ilaf Quraysh ilafihim﴾. The reciters of the major regional centres, with the exception of Abu Ja'far, read both the ﴿ilaf﴾ and the ﴿ilafihim﴾ with a yā' after the hamza. Abu Ja'far agreed with the others on ﴿ilaf﴾, reading it with a yā' after the hamza, but there are different reports about his reading of ﴿ilafihim﴾. It is reported from him that he read it as "ilfihim" (إلْفِهِمْ), taking it as a verbal noun from alifa, yaʾlafu, ilfan, without a yā'. Some have related from him that he read it as "ilafihim" (إلافِهِمْ), without a yā' and with a short alif.

The correct reading in my view is the one that reads both with the yā' after the hamza, from ʾalaftu al-shay'a, ʾulifuhu, ilafan, because the reciters, who are the authoritative body, agree upon it. The Arabs have two usages: ʾalaftu and alaftu. Whoever says ʾalaftu with a long alif says "fa-ana ʾuʾālifu ilafan" (I am making a covenant); whoever says alaftu with a short alif says "fa-ana ʾālifu ilfan", and he is a man who is ʾālif ilfan (accustomed). It is related from ʿIkrimah that he used to read it: "li-tuʾlifa Quraysh ilfahum rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf" (that Quraysh may become accustomed to their journey of winter and summer).

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated this to me, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Makin, from ʿIkrimah.

It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ concerning this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting: "ilfahum rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf".

The grammarians (ahl al-ʿarabiyya) disagreed about the meaning that brings in this lām in His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: what governs it is His words ﴿so He made them like eaten chaff﴾. According to this view, the lām is connected to His words "made them", so the meaning of the speech must be: We did this to the People of the Elephant as a favour from Us to the people of this House and as a kindness from Us to them, in addition to Our favour upon them in the journey of winter and summer. Thus the lām in ﴿li-ilaf﴾ would mean "ilā" (to), as if it were said: a favour for a favour, and to a favour, because ilā stands in the place of lām and lām stands in the place of ilā.

Some of the exegetes (ahl al-taʾwil, those who interpret the Qur'an) have stated this view.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿ilafihim rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf﴾, who said: Their covenant to it, so that the journey of winter or summer does not burden them.

⁕ Isma'il ibn Musa al-Sudi narrated to me, saying: Sharik informed us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid: ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, who said: My favour upon Quraysh.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Hilali narrated to me, saying: Farwa ibn Abi al-Maghra' al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAmir ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, who said: My favour upon Quraysh.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: This view has been stated, and it is said that He, blessed and exalted, made His Prophet ﷺ marvel, so He said: Marvel, O Muhammad, at the blessings of God upon Quraysh, in their covenant of the journey of winter and summer. Then He said: Let them not occupy themselves with that from faith and from following you; the proof is in His words ﴿so let them worship the Lord of this House﴾.

Some of the exegetes directed the interpretation of His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾ toward the mutual affection of some of them for others.

Those who said so:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of God ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, and he recited ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the People of the Elephant?﴾ up to the end of the surah, and said: This is for the covenant of Quraysh. I did this to them for the affection of Quraysh, lest I disperse their affection and their union, and the People of the Elephant came only to seize their sacred ones; so God did that.

The correct statement on this matter, in our view, is that this lām carries the meaning of wonder (taʿajjub), and that the meaning of the speech is: Marvel at the covenant of Quraysh in the journey of winter and summer, and their abandoning the worship of the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear. So let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear. When the Arabs bring this lām into speech for wonder, they suffice with it as evidence of wonder at the appearance of the verb that it governs, as the poet said:

Did it deceive you that they called Qurrah a poet?
Alas for their fathers, from a ʿarif and a poet!

So He suffices with the lām as evidence of wonder at the appearance of the verb, and the speech is in fact: "Did it deceive you that they said: Marvel at Qurrah, a poet?" Likewise His words ﴿li-ilaf﴾.

As for the view we have reported, that it is connected to His words ﴿so He made them like eaten chaff﴾, if that were so, then ﴿li-ilaf﴾ would have to be part of ﴿Have you not considered﴾, and the surah would not be a separate surah from ﴿Have you not considered﴾. The consensus of all Muslims that they are two complete surahs, each separate from the other, demonstrates the invalidity of the view of those who said that. Moreover, if His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾ were connected to His words ﴿so He made them like eaten chaff﴾, then ﴿Have you not considered﴾ would not be complete until it was joined to ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, because the speech is not complete except with the completion of the report that was mentioned.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿ilafahum rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf﴾, he said: their adherence.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, he said: He forbade them from the journey and commanded them to worship the Lord of this House, and He spared them the burden. Their journeys were in winter and summer, so they had no rest in winter or summer. Then He fed them after that against hunger, and secured them against fear, and they became accustomed to the journey, so when they wished they travelled, and when they wished they stayed. That was among God's favours upon them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿAbd al-Ala narrated to me, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: Quraysh had become accustomed to Busra and Yemen, going to this one in winter and to that one in summer. ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House﴾: so He commanded them to remain in Mecca.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh ilafihim﴾, who said: They were merchants, so God knew their love for Syria.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, who said: The custom of Quraysh is their custom of the journey of winter and summer.

⁕ I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾: they had become accustomed to travelling in the heat of summer and in winter.

* *

As for His words ﴿ilafihim﴾: it is in the genitive by substitution (badal), as if He said: for the covenant of Quraysh, for their covenant, the journey of winter and summer. As for ﴿rihlah﴾, it is put in the accusative by ﴿ilafihim﴾, which takes it as its object.

* *

As for His words ﴿rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf﴾: it means the journey of Quraysh, the two journeys: one to Syria in summer and the other to Yemen in winter.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf﴾: They had two journeys: the summer to Syria, and the winter to Yemen for trade. When winter came, Syria was closed to them because of the cold, so their journey in winter was to Yemen.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, concerning ﴿rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf﴾, who said: They were merchants.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan; Ibn ʿAbd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Kalbi, concerning ﴿rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf﴾, who said: They had two journeys: a journey in winter to Yemen, and a journey in summer to Syria.

⁕ ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAmir ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning ﴿ilafihim rihlat al-shitaʾ wa al-sayf﴾, who said: They used to spend winter in Mecca and summer in al-Ta'if.

* *

As for His words ﴿so let them worship the Lord of this House﴾:

It means: let them remain in their place and homeland of Mecca, and let them worship the Lord of this House, meaning by the House: the Ka'ba.

As follows:

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, prayed the maghrib prayer in Mecca and recited ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, and when he reached His words ﴿so let them worship the Lord of this House﴾ he pointed with his hand toward the House.

⁕ ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAmir ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿so let them worship the Lord of this House﴾, he said: the Ka'ba.

Some of them said: They were commanded to become accustomed to worshipping the Lord of Mecca just as they had become accustomed to the two journeys.

Those who said so:

⁕ ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Amuli narrated to us, saying: Marwan narrated to us, from ʿAsim al-Ahwal, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning the words of God ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh﴾, he said: They were commanded to become accustomed to worshipping the Lord of this House, as they were accustomed to the journey of winter and summer.

* *

As for His words ﴿alladhi ʾat'amahum min jū'﴾ (who fed them against hunger):

It means: who fed Quraysh against hunger.

As follows:

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿who fed them against hunger﴾: meaning, Quraysh of Mecca, by the supplication of Abraham ﷺ, when he said ﴿and provide them with fruits﴾.

﴿And secured them against fear﴾: the exegetes differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿and secured them against fear﴾. Some said: the meaning is that He secured them from what those outside the sanctuary feared, from raids, wars, fighting, and matters over which the Arabs feared one another.

Those who said so:

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿and secured them against fear﴾: when Abraham, peace be upon him, said ﴿My Lord, make this land secure﴾.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿and secured them against fear﴾, who said: He secured them from every enemy within their sanctuary.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿li-ilaf Quraysh ilafihim﴾, who said: The people of Mecca were merchants who alternated this in winter and summer, secure among the Arabs, while the Arabs raided one another and could not do so against them, nor could they manage it, out of fear. Even if a man of them was struck in one of the Arab quarters, when someone said "a man of the sanctuary (Hirmi)" he was left alone along with his property, in honour of that, for the security God had given them.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, ﴿and secured them against fear﴾, who said: They used to say: We are of the sanctuary of God, so no one would confront them in the Jahiliyya, and they were secure by that; but other tribes of the Arabs, when they went out, were raided.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿and secured them against fear﴾: The Arabs raided one another and took one another captive, but they were secure from that because of the sanctuary. And he recited: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which the fruits of every thing are brought?﴾

Others said: What is meant by this is: and He secured them from leprosy.

Those who said so:

⁕ al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all saying: al-Dahhak said: ﴿and secured them against fear﴾: from their fear of leprosy.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, ﴿and secured them against fear﴾, who said: from leprosy and other things.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' said: I heard "who fed them against hunger": hunger. "And secured them against fear": fear is leprosy.

⁕ ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAmir ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Khattab ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿and secured them against fear﴾, he said: The fear is leprosy.

The correct statement on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that He ﴿secured them against fear﴾, and the enemy is a thing feared, and leprosy is a thing feared. God did not specify the report that He secured them from the enemy to the exclusion of leprosy, nor from leprosy to the exclusion of the enemy; rather He made the report general. So the correct view is that it should be general as He, exalted is His remembrance, made it general, and thus it is said: He secured them from both of these things.

End of the exegesis of Surat Quraysh.
